en: person who helps bring something about

examples.en: He took on the role of founder of the new group.

examples.ko: 두 회사 합병의 산파역은 그 변호사였어요.
examples.en: The lawyer was the one who brought about the two companies' merger.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 산파역으로 나서서 문제가 풀렸어요.
examples.en: He stepped in as a go-between and the problem was solved.
Thanks to the person who got it started, our club was created.

examples.ko: 산파역이 없었다면 이 행사는 열리지 못했을 거예요.
examples.en: Without the person who set it in motion, this event could not have been held.

examples.ko: 두 사람을 소개해 주는 산파역을 했어요.
examples.en: I played the role of matchmaker by introducing the two.

explain: 아기를 받는 사람보다는 어떤 일이 생겨나도록 앞에서 도와준 사람을 비유할 때 많이 써요. '산파역을 맡다/하다'처럼 말하고 칭찬하는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스나 인터뷰에서 새로운 모임, 계약, 합의가 만들어진 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 선생님이 우리 동아리의 산파 역할을 했어요.
phrases.en: That teacher played the role of midwife for our club.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산파역'과 같은 뜻인데 '역할'을 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '산파역', with '역할' spelled out.
phrases.en_equiv: role as a midwife of something

phrases.example: 언니가 우리 가게를 여는 데 산파역을 맡았어요.
phrases.en: My older sister took on the role of midwife in opening our shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 생기도록 앞에서 이끌고 도와주는 역할을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone takes the lead in helping something come into being.
phrases.en_equiv: to take on the midwife role

phrases.example: 그 책이 새로운 제도의 산파역이 되었어요.
phrases.en: That book became the midwife of the new system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 책이나 사건이 시작의 계기가 되었을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used for a book or event that triggered a beginning.

explain_en: It is more often used figuratively for a person who helped bring something into being than for someone who delivers babies. You say '산파역을 맡다/하다', and it carries a praising tone. It often appears in news and interviews about how a new group, contract or agreement came about.

examples.en: My father graduated from a commercial high school and worked at a bank.
At a commercial high school you learn accounting and management.
There are many seniors at the company who went to commercial high school.
I earned a certificate while attending a commercial high school.
I heard commercial high schools were popular in the past.

examples.ko: 상고 때 친구들과 아직도 자주 만나요.
examples.en: I still often meet my friends from commercial high school.

explain: '공고', '농고'처럼 학교 종류의 첫 글자를 따서 부르는 말이에요. 법원에서 쓰는 '상고'(윗법원에 다시 재판을 요청하는 일)는 소리만 같고 뜻이 전혀 달라요.

phrases.en: My younger brother attends a commercial high school and learns accounting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 학교의 학생이라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being a student at that kind of school.
phrases.en_equiv: to attend a commercial high school

phrases.example: 그분은 상고 출신이지만 큰 회사 사장이 됐어요.
phrases.en: He graduated from a commercial high school but became the head of a big company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 학교를 졸업했는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which school someone graduated from.

phrases.en: At a commercial high school, you learn business and management.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상고'의 원래 이름이고 조금 더 정확한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full name of 상고, a bit more formal and precise.

explain_en: Like 공고 and 농고, it takes the first syllable of the school type, here 상업고등학교. The 상고 used in courts, asking a higher court to review a case, only sounds the same and means something completely different.

examples.ko: 장마에도 시장 상인들은 생업을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: Even in the rainy season, market merchants kept up their livelihood.

examples.ko: 그는 생업을 잠시 접고 가족을 돌봤어요.
examples.en: He put his trade aside for a while and cared for his family.
Farming is the livelihood of the people in this village.

examples.ko: 생업에 바빠서 모임에 거의 못 나와요.
examples.en: I'm busy making a living, so I rarely come to meetings.

examples.ko: 큰 눈 때문에 생업에 지장이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The heavy snow disrupted people's livelihoods.

examples.ko: 저는 작은 가게를 생업으로 삼아 오래 일했어요.
examples.en: I worked for a long time with a small shop as my livelihood.

explain: '생업'은 먹고살기 위해 하는 일이에요. '직업'보다 '생계'에 무게가 있어서 '생업에 종사하다', '생업을 이어 가다'처럼 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요. 취미나 부업은 생업이라고 하지 않아요.

phrases.en: The villagers make their living at sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 자주 쓰는 격식 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal collocation often seen in news and writing.
phrases.en_equiv: to be engaged in one's trade

phrases.en: He makes farming his livelihood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일로 먹고산다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say what someone earns a living by.

phrases.en: He supports his family's living on his own.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생업'이 일 자체라면 '생계'는 먹고사는 형편을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 'saengeop' is the work itself, 'saenggye' refers to making a living.

explain_en: Work that supports survival; somewhat literary (농사를 생업으로) 생업 is the work you do to make a living. It leans toward 생계 (the means of living) more than 직업 does, and it appears in news and writing as 생업에 종사하다 and 생업을 이어 가다. A hobby or side job is not called 생업.

dis.h: work one depends on to survive

p.n: 직업 is neutral; 생업 stresses that this is how he makes his living.

t90.ax: The heavy snow disrupted people's livelihoods.

examples.en: The designer of this bridge is a foreigner.
The designer revised the drawing again.

examples.ko: 건물 설계자를 직접 만나 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to meet the building's designer in person.

examples.ko: 그는 이 도시를 만든 설계자로 불려요.
examples.en: He is called the designer who created this city.
The designer's ideas show all over the building.
I had a meeting with the program's designer.

explain: 건물, 다리, 기계, 시스템의 구조를 계획하는 사람이에요. 옷이나 포스터를 꾸미는 사람은 '디자이너'라고 하고, 설계자는 구조와 계획 쪽에 써요. 건축 쪽에서는 '건축가'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The designer of this building is a famous architect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물의 구조를 계획한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who planned the structure of a building.

phrases.en: I am the system designer of this app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 프로그램이나 시스템의 구조를 계획하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who plans the structure of a program or system.

phrases.en: If you are curious, ask the designer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 뒤에 '에게'를 붙여 대상을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에게 after a person to mark who you ask.

explain_en: Person who designs buildings, bridges or systems (다리의 설계자) A 설계자 plans the structure of buildings, bridges, machines or systems. Someone who styles clothes or posters is a 디자이너. In architecture you will also hear 건축가.

t90.ax: The designer revised the drawing again.

examples.ko: 그는 고전부터 현대 소설까지 다 섭렵했어요.
examples.en: He has read everything from the classics to modern novels.

examples.ko: 방학 동안 이 분야의 책을 모두 섭렵하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work through all the books in this field during the vacation.
He is a chef who has mastered the cuisines of many countries.

examples.ko: 한 번에 다 섭렵하려고 하면 금방 지쳐요.
examples.en: If you try to cover everything at once, you get tired quickly.

examples.ko: 그 감독의 영화를 섭렵해 보니 스타일이 보였어요.
examples.en: After going through that director's films, I could see his style.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 발라드와 록을 두루 섭렵했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that singer has covered both ballads and rock thoroughly.

explain: 책, 장르, 작품처럼 여러 개를 두루 접해서 많이 안다는 느낌으로 써요. 하나만 깊이 공부할 때는 '파고들다'가 더 어울리고, '섭렵하다'는 폭넓게 훑는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: He has read widely in both Eastern and Western philosophy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '두루'는 널리라는 뜻이라서 폭넓게 접했다는 느낌이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: 두루 means widely, which makes the sense of broad coverage clearer.

phrases.example: 이번 여름에 한국 고전을 섭렵해 볼 거예요.
phrases.en: This summer I'm going to try making my way through Korean classics.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙여 도전하는 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보다' expresses a plan to try it out.

phrases.example: 방학 동안 여러 분야의 책을 폭넓게 읽었어요.
phrases.en: During vacation I read widely across many fields.
phrases.nuance_ko: '섭렵하다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, more everyday way to say it.

explain_en: It is used for going through many things such as books, genres or works and coming to know a lot of them. For studying just one thing deeply, '파고들다' fits better, while '섭렵하다' has a feel of covering a wide range.

en: to belong to; to be affiliated

examples.en: I belong to the sales team.
Which team did that player belong to?
It's a research institute affiliated with a university.
Where are you affiliated now?
If you belong to a company, you get insurance.
I'm anxious because I don't belong to anywhere yet.

explain: '~에 소속하다'는 조직에 속해 있다는 뜻인데, 말할 때는 '~에 속해 있다'나 '~ 소속이다'를 더 많이 써요. 소개할 때도 '○○ 소속이에요'처럼 명사로 써요. 소속하다는 글이나 공식적인 말에 가까워요.

phrases.en: I belong to the sales team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기소개나 공식적인 자리에서 명사로 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say it, using a noun in introductions and formal settings.

phrases.en: My friend is part of the sales team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '소속하다' 대신 더 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural everyday alternative to 소속하다.

phrases.en: Which team does that player belong to?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에 속하는지 물을 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for asking which group someone belongs to.

explain_en: Rarer active form; formal, official affiliation. The pattern is ~에 소속하다, but in speech people more often say ~에 속해 있다 or ~ 소속이다. When introducing yourself you use the noun, like '○○ 소속이에요'. The verb itself sounds written or official.

dis.h: active form, rarer; belong to organization
gh: be affiliated with an organization; passive form

t90.ax: I belong to the sales team.

examples.ko: 그 마을에는 도자기를 만드는 수공업자가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many craftsmen who make pottery in that village.

examples.ko: 수공업자들은 직접 손으로 물건을 만들어 팔았어요.
examples.en: The craftsmen made things by hand and sold them.
Bags made by craftsmen are known for being sturdy.
Craftsmen in the old days worked while helping each other.
My father is a craftsman who runs a small shop.
As machines appeared, the craftsmen's work decreased.

explain: '장인'은 솜씨가 뛰어난 사람을 높여 부르는 말이고, '수공업자'는 손으로 물건을 만들어 먹고사는 사람을 가리키는 중립적인 말이에요. 역사나 경제 설명에서 주로 나와요.

phrases.example: 그는 어릴 때부터 수공업자가 되고 싶었어요.
phrases.en: He wanted to become a craftsman from a young age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 '이/가 되다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 이/가 되다 to talk about becoming one.

phrases.en: He works as a craftsman in the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로 일하다'를 붙여 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 으로 일하다 to say what someone does for a living.

phrases.en: Many craftsmen lived in medieval cities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 시대 이름과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with a period name in history talk.

explain_en: Person who makes goods by hand for a living. '장인' is a respectful word for a person of outstanding skill, while '수공업자' is a neutral word for someone who makes a living by making things by hand. It mostly appears in history and economics explanations.

t90.ax: My father is a craftsman who runs a small shop.

examples.en: I want to study veterinary science at university.

examples.ko: 수의학과에 들어가려면 점수가 아주 높아야 해요.
examples.en: You need very high scores to get into the veterinary department.
A friend who majored in veterinary science opened an animal hospital.
I hear that in veterinary science you learn about cows and horses too.
Veterinary science is popular these days because there are more pets.

examples.ko: 형은 수의학 박사 과정에 다니고 있어요.
examples.en: My older brother is in a doctoral program in veterinary science.

explain: 동물의 병을 보는 사람은 '수의사'라고 하고, 사람의 병을 다루는 공부는 '의학'이라고 해요. 대학에서는 '수의학과'나 '수의과대학'이라는 이름을 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is in the veterinary science department.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에서 수의학을 배우는 학과 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the university department that teaches veterinary science.

phrases.en: I like animals, so I study veterinary science.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학문으로 배운다는 뜻으로 '공부하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 공부하다 to mean studying it as a subject.

phrases.example: 오늘 수의학 수업에서 강아지 몸을 배웠어요.
phrases.en: In today's veterinary science class, we learned about a dog's body.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수업', '책'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can go before other nouns like 수업 (class) or 책 (book).

explain_en: A person who treats animal illnesses is called a '수의사' (veterinarian), while the study of human illness is '의학' (medicine). At universities you will see the names '수의학과' or '수의과대학'.

examples.en: I carry out important work at the company.
The team carried out the mission safely.
I want to perform my role well.
There is not enough time to carry out the assignment.
The result differs depending on who carries it out.
We carried it out as planned and succeeded.

explain: '하다'보다 딱딱하고, 맡은 임무나 과제를 끝까지 해낸다는 느낌이에요. '수행평가'는 학교에서 수업 중 과제를 평가하는 말이에요. 일, 임무, 역할, 과제와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I carry out the role of leader on the team.
phrases.nuance_ko: '역할'과 함께 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation with 역할 (role).

phrases.en: Students carry out the assignment during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 주어진 과제를 해낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means completing an assigned task at school.

phrases.en: I managed to finish the hard job to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수행하다'보다 쉬운 말이고, 어려운 일을 끝까지 잘 마쳤다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 수행하다, and it carries the feel of successfully finishing something difficult.

explain_en: A person carries out an assigned task to the end. It is stiffer than the plain verb for doing, with a sense of carrying an assigned task through. A related school word names in-class performance assessment. It pairs well with work, mission, role and assignment.

dis.h: carry out a task or duty
gh: carry out laws, budgets, or sentences
boldly carry out a drastic measure

p.n: 실시하다 stresses putting a planned survey into effect.

t90.ax: I want to perform my role well.

en: to become proficient; to become skilled

examples.en: A skilled technician fixed the machine right away.

examples.ko: 일을 오래 하면 손이 숙련돼서 훨씬 빨라져요.
examples.en: If you work for a long time, your hands become practiced and much faster.
I'm not proficient yet, so I make a lot of mistakes.

examples.ko: 이 일에 숙련되기까지 보통 몇 년이 걸려요.
examples.en: It usually takes a few years to become proficient at this job.

examples.ko: 그 요리사는 칼질이 정말 숙련돼 보여요.
examples.en: That chef's knife work looks really practiced.
After practicing for a long time, I'm now quite proficient.

explain: '숙련된 기술자', '숙련된 솜씨'처럼 사람이나 솜씨를 꾸미는 말로 많이 써요. '능숙하다'는 익숙하고 솜씨가 좋다는 느낌이고, '숙련되다'는 연습과 경험으로 그렇게 된 과정이 느껴져요. 반대말은 '미숙하다'예요.

phrases.en: Everyone was amazed by the grandmother's skilled work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜 경험으로 얻은 솜씨를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise skill gained through long experience.

phrases.en: I practice every day until I become proficient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표가 되는 상태를 말할 때 연결형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for the state one is aiming for.

phrases.en: I'm not yet proficient, so I make many mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 익숙하지 않다는 뜻의 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form meaning not yet experienced enough.

explain_en: Skilled through long experience in work or machines. It is often used to describe people or skills, as in '숙련된 기술자' or '숙련된 솜씨'. '능숙하다' simply says someone is smooth and good at something, while '숙련되다' carries the sense of having become so through practice and experience. The opposite is '미숙하다'.

t90.ax: That chef's knife work looks really practiced.

en: to train; to educate; to nurture

examples.en: This school trains excellent cooks.

examples.ko: 정부가 젊은 과학자를 양성하려고 지원금을 줬어요.
examples.en: The government gave funding to nurture young scientists.
I want to attend a university that trains teachers.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 신입 사원을 전문가로 양성했어요.
examples.en: Our company trained its new employees to become experts.

examples.ko: 축구 선수를 양성할 학원이 우리 동네에 생겼어요.
examples.en: An academy to train soccer players opened in our neighborhood.
It takes a long time to develop talented people.

explain: '가르치다'는 지식을 알려 주는 것이고, '양성하다'는 어떤 일을 할 사람으로 키워 내는 것이에요. 목적어는 사람이고 '인재', '전문가', '선수'와 자주 같이 써요. 집에서 아이를 키울 때는 '키우다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 이 대학은 나라에 필요한 인재를 양성해요.
phrases.en: This university trains the talent the country needs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인재', '전문가', '선수'와 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, used with words like talent, experts, and athletes.

phrases.example: 저희 학원은 어린 선수를 양성하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our academy is training young athletes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 이어지는 일을 말할 때 '-고 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -고 있다 to describe an ongoing effort.

phrases.example: 그 학교는 훌륭한 음악가를 많이 키워 냈어요.
phrases.en: That school has produced many fine musicians.
phrases.nuance_ko: '양성하다'보다 말할 때 더 편하게 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual, spoken alternative to 양성하다.

explain_en: Schools or institutions raising experts in a field. '가르치다' means to teach knowledge, while '양성하다' means to raise people into those who can do a certain job. The object is a person, often '인재' (talent), '전문가' (expert), or '선수' (athlete). For raising a child at home, use '키우다'.

gh: make someone or an animal practice
cultivate skill or discipline, martial arts

p.n: 양성 means producing professionals; 훈련시키다 means drilling skills.

examples.en: He served as minister twice.
This is a person who served as a professor and department chair.
The person who long served as chairman stepped down.
After holding a number of posts, he retired.

examples.ko: 시장을 역임할 때 도로를 많이 만들었어요.
examples.en: While serving as mayor, he built many roads.
I hear he has a lot of experience from having served as CEO.

explain: 회사나 정부에서 높은 직책을 차례로 맡았다는 뜻이라 소개 글이나 뉴스에서 써요. 지금 하는 일에는 쓰지 않고 이미 지난 경력에 써요. 일상 말로는 '~을 했어요', '~로 일했어요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My father served as mayor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높이는 사람의 경력을 말할 때 '-시-'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-시-' to honor the person whose career you describe.

phrases.en: I met a person who had served as principal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 사람을 꾸미는 활용형으로 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form used when introducing someone.

phrases.en: He was the alumni association president for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '역임하다'보다 부드러운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, everyday alternative to '역임하다'.

explain_en: It means someone took on high positions one after another in a company or government, so it appears in profiles and the news. It is used for past career history, not for the job someone is doing now. In everyday speech people say '~을 했어요' or '~로 일했어요'.

examples.en: My father is a welder who works at a shipyard.
The welder joins steel plates, sparks flying.
You need a certificate to become a welder.
My uncle is a welder with twenty years of experience.

examples.ko: 용접공은 보호 안경을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: Welders must wear protective goggles.

examples.ko: 현장에서 용접공 두 명이 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: Two welders are working at the site.

explain: 직업을 말할 때는 '용접공이에요'라고도 하고 '용접 일을 해요'라고도 해요. 기술 직업 이름에 붙는 '-공'은 기술자를 나타내요. 현장 이야기나 구인 공고에서 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: My uncle works as a welder in a factory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to state someone's job.

phrases.example: 저는 십 년째 용접 일을 해요.
phrases.en: I have done welding work for ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람보다 하는 일에 초점을 둔 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the work rather than the person.

phrases.en: He is a skilled welding technician.
phrases.nuance_ko: '용접공'과 같은 직업을 조금 더 풀어서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more descriptive name for the same job.

explain_en: To say the job you can say '용접공이에요' or '용접 일을 해요'. The '-공' ending marks a skilled worker. You often see it in talk about work sites and in job ads.

en: to lead; to guide; to escort

examples.en: The teacher led the students to the museum.
A travel agency staff member is leading the tourists.

examples.ko: 제가 아이들을 인솔할 테니 걱정 마세요.
examples.en: I'll take charge of the children, so don't worry.
Leading a group is harder than you'd think.

examples.ko: 제가 인솔한 학생은 모두 열 명이에요.
examples.en: The students I led number ten in all.

examples.ko: 소풍 때 반 아이들을 인솔하며 길을 건넜어요.
examples.en: On the picnic, I crossed the road leading the class.

explain: '데리고 가다'와 달리 선생님, 가이드처럼 단체를 책임지고 이끌 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '데리고 가요'가 더 자연스럽고, 이끄는 사람은 '인솔자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The group leader looked after the students throughout the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단체를 책임지고 이끄는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who takes charge of and leads a group.

phrases.example: 소풍에는 인솔 교사 세 분이 같이 가요.
phrases.en: Three supervising teachers go along on the field trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생들과 함께 가며 이끄는 선생님을 뜻하고 학교 행사에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A teacher who accompanies and leads students, common in school events.

phrases.en: Mom took the child to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '인솔하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday alternative to 인솔하다.

explain_en: Lead a group like students on a trip. Unlike '데리고 가다', it is used when someone such as a teacher or guide takes responsibility for leading a group. In casual talk '데리고 가요' sounds more natural, and the person in charge is called '인솔자'.

dis.h: lead a group on a trip
gh: direct or command, e.g. an orchestra
lead people or a team, general

p.n: 인솔 is formal and means accompanying a group; 이끌다 is general leading.

t90.ax: The students I led number ten in all.
